questions.stem: He was accused ___ theft.
questions.explanation: 'Accuse somebody OF something'; 'charge' takes 'with'.

questions.stem: She is deprived ___ her rights.
questions.explanation: 'Deprive somebody OF something' is the fixed pattern.

questions.stem: He is addicted ___ gambling.
questions.explanation: 'Addicted to' — the 'to' here is a preposition, so a gerund follows.

questions.stem: The teacher was pleased ___ my result.
questions.explanation: 'Pleased with' is used for a person or thing; 'pleased at' suits news or an event.

questions.stem: He has no control ___ his temper.
questions.explanation: 'Control over' is the standard collocation.

questions.stem: She is confident ___ her success.
questions.explanation: 'Confident of' something, though 'confident about' is also heard.

questions.stem: I am accustomed ___ getting up early.
questions.explanation: 'Accustomed to' takes a gerund because 'to' is a preposition here.

questions.stem: He is afraid ___ dogs.
questions.explanation: 'Afraid of' is the fixed form.

questions.stem: The meeting will begin ___ 10 a.m.
questions.explanation: 'At' is used with a clock time.

questions.stem: Scarcely had he arrived ___ the train left.
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely/hardly … when' and 'no sooner … than' are the fixed pairs.

questions.stem: No sooner had he seen me ___ he ran away.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner' is always completed by 'than'.

questions.stem: He said that he ___ the book already.
questions.explanation: After a past reporting verb the present perfect shifts to the past perfect.

questions.stem: I ___ here for five years before I moved to Dhaka.
questions.explanation: Of two past events, the earlier one takes the past perfect.

questions.stem: She ___ her homework before her father came home.
questions.explanation: The action completed before another past action takes the past perfect.

questions.stem: Look! The baby ___ .
questions.explanation: 'Look!' signals something happening right now, so the present continuous is used.

questions.stem: They ___ in this house since 2010.
questions.explanation: 'Since' with an ongoing state calls for the present perfect.

questions.stem: The sun ___ in the east.
questions.explanation: A universal truth takes the simple present.

questions.stem: She ___ to the market an hour ago.
questions.explanation: 'An hour ago' fixes a definite past time, so the simple past is used.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'They will have completed the work.'
options: The work will be completed by them.
The work will have been completed by them.
The work has been completed by them.
The work would be completed by them.
questions.explanation: Future perfect active becomes 'will have been + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'Somebody has stolen my bag.'
options: My bag was stolen by somebody.
questions.explanation: Present perfect active becomes 'has/have been + past participle'; an indefinite agent is dropped.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'Do not touch the wire.'
options: Let not the wire be touched.
Do not let the wire touch.
questions.explanation: A negative imperative becomes 'Let not + object + be + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into active: 'The letter was being written by him.'
questions.explanation: 'Was being + past participle' corresponds to the past continuous active.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'People speak English all over the world.'
options: English is spoken all over the world.
English was spoken all over the world.
English is being spoken all over the world.
English has spoken all over the world.
questions.explanation: A general truth in the simple present becomes 'is/are + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'He gave me a pen.'
options: A pen gave me by him.
I was given a pen by him.
I am given a pen by him.
A pen was giving to me.
questions.explanation: With two objects, either may become the subject; 'I was given a pen' is the usual form.

questions.stem: Change into passive: 'The boy killed the snake.'
options: The snake killed by the boy.
The snake was killed by the boy.
The snake is killed by the boy.
The snake has killed by the boy.
questions.explanation: Simple past active becomes 'was/were + past participle'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Do not go there."
options: He told me not to go there.
He said me not to go there.
He asked me that I should not go there.
He requested me not going there.
questions.explanation: A negative imperative becomes 'forbade' or 'told … not to + verb'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "Let us play cricket."
options: He said that we should play cricket.
He proposed that we should play cricket.
He told us to play cricket.
questions.explanation: 'Let us' expressing a suggestion becomes 'proposed/suggested that … should'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: She said to him, "May you be happy!"
options: She said that he might be happy.
She wished that he might be happy.
She told him to be happy.
She asked whether he was happy.
questions.explanation: An optative sentence takes a reporting verb of wishing: 'wished that … might'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said to me, "Are you happy?"
options: He asked me if I was happy.
He asked me if I am happy.
He said me whether I was happy.
He asked me was I happy.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with 'if' or 'whether' and statement word order.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: The teacher said to us, "Work hard."
options: The teacher told us to work hard.
The teacher said us to work hard.
The teacher asked us that we work hard.
The teacher requested us working hard.
questions.explanation: An imperative becomes 'told/ordered + object + to-infinitive'.

questions.stem: Change into indirect speech: He said, "I am reading a book."
options: He said that he is reading a book.
He said that he was reading a book.
He says that he was reading a book.
He told that he is reading a book.
questions.explanation: The present continuous shifts to the past continuous after a past reporting verb.

questions.stem: ‘তার বাবা মারা গেছেন’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: বর্তমানে বেঁচে নেই বোঝাতে ইংরেজিতে 'is dead' ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘আমার একটি কলম আছে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: অধিকার বোঝাতে 'have' ব্যবহৃত হয়।

questions.stem: ‘সে তিন বছর যাবৎ এখানে কাজ করছে’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
options: He works here for three years.
He is working here for three years.
He has been working here for three years.
questions.explanation: ‘যাবৎ’ অর্থাৎ কাজটি চলমান — present perfect continuous।

questions.stem: ‘দরজাটি বন্ধ কর’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: আদেশ বোঝাতে imperative বাক্য — কর্তা উহ্য থাকে।

questions.stem: ‘আকাশ মেঘলা’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: ‘মেঘলা’ একটি বিশেষণ — cloudy।

questions.stem: ‘আমি ভাত খাচ্ছি’ — এর সঠিক ইংরেজি অনুবাদ কোনটি?
questions.explanation: এখন চলছে এমন কাজ — present continuous।

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: The scenery of Kashmir are beautiful.
The sceneries of Kashmir are beautiful.
The scenery of Kashmir is beautiful.
The scenery of Kashmir were beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is uncountable and takes a singular verb; 'sceneries' is not standard.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: He is more junior than me.
questions.explanation: Latin comparatives such as junior and senior take 'to', never 'than'.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Privilege' has no 'd' — a very common misspelling.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: The noun drops the 'i' of 'maintain': maintenance.

questions.stem: Which sentence is correct?
options: I have finished my work yesterday.
I had finished my work yesterday.
questions.explanation: The present perfect cannot be used with a definite past time such as 'yesterday'.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Occurrence' doubles both the r and the c.

questions.stem: Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: 'Definitely' contains the word 'finite'.

questions.stem: In 'He is a man of letters', the phrase 'of letters' functions as a —
questions.explanation: It qualifies the noun 'man', so it works as an adjective phrase.

questions.stem: In 'Swimming is a good exercise', the word 'swimming' is a —
questions.explanation: A verb form in -ing used as a noun is a gerund.

questions.stem: In 'Gold is a precious metal', the word 'gold' is a —
questions.explanation: A noun naming a substance or material is a material noun.

questions.stem: In 'He works hard but earns little', the word 'but' is a —
questions.explanation: 'But' joins two clauses, so it is a conjunction.

questions.stem: In 'This is my book', the word 'my' is a —
questions.explanation: It qualifies the noun 'book' while showing possession, so it is a possessive adjective.

questions.stem: In 'She sings sweetly', the word 'sweetly' is a —
questions.explanation: It modifies the verb 'sings', so it is an adverb of manner.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'pragmatic'.
questions.explanation: 'Pragmatic' means dealing with things in a practical rather than theoretical way.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'lucid'.
questions.explanation: 'Lucid' means easily understood, i.e. clear.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'humble'.
questions.explanation: 'Humble' means modest; its opposite is 'arrogant'.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'barren'.
questions.explanation: 'Barren' land produces nothing; 'fertile' land produces abundantly.

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to 'vacant'.
questions.explanation: 'Vacant' means unoccupied or empty.

questions.stem: Choose the opposite of 'victory'.
questions.explanation: 'Victory' and 'defeat' are direct opposites.

questions.stem: 'To carry coals to Newcastle' means —
questions.explanation: Newcastle was a coal-producing town, so taking coal there is pointless.

questions.stem: 'To bell the cat' means —
questions.explanation: From the fable of the mice — it means to take on a dangerous task for the common good.

questions.stem: 'At one's wits' end' means —
questions.explanation: It means being so perplexed that one does not know what to do next.

questions.stem: 'To make both ends meet' means —
questions.explanation: It means to manage on the money one has.

questions.stem: 'By and by' means —
questions.explanation: 'By and by' means before long or gradually.

questions.stem: He proposed that the meeting ___ postponed.
questions.explanation: After 'propose/suggest that', the subjunctive base form is used.

questions.stem: Had I been rich, I ___ a car.
questions.explanation: 'Had + past participle' signals the third conditional, completed by 'would have + past participle'.

questions.stem: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Subjects ending in -ics are singular despite the final s.

questions.stem: He is used to ___ early.
questions.explanation: In 'be used to', 'to' is a preposition and takes a gerund.

questions.stem: Let him ___ the work.
questions.explanation: 'Let' is followed by the bare infinitive.

questions.stem: The boys ___ playing in the field.
questions.explanation: A plural subject takes a plural verb.
